newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM reiterates commitment to logging ban.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM reiterates commitment to logging ban.

text.p: Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Tuesday reiterated his commitment to maintain a ban on log exports.
"I will refuse to sign any agreement allowing the export of any logs," he said when asked about media reports that Thailand would press Cambodia to relax its timber export ban.

Ranariddh, speaking to reporters at the launch of a river ferry, also said he had received a letter from Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet on Monday saying Hanoi was willing to help Cambodia stop the illegal export of logs into Vietnam.
The prince's remarks coincide with a visit by International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials to review Cambodia's forestry policy before deciding on the fate of $40 million in loans.
The IMF cancelled a $20 million payment last year over the logging issue.
The government has said it has attempted to improve its forestry policy, including implementing a December 31 ban on all new logging and timber exports.

But the British environmental group Global Witness said on Monday logging was continuing unabated. It alleged continued government involvement in illegal logging and questioned the administration's commitment to reforming forestry policy.
Ranariddh urged the IMF to be reasonable and extend the next $20 million tranche of a three-year $120 million loan, half of which has been disbursed.
"I hope that the IMF will resume its support to us," he said.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen warned last week that Cambodia would be forced to resume cutting and selling logs to pay its civil servants if the IMF stopped the loan.
But Finance Minister Keat Chhon, acknowledging continuing illegal logging, said on Monday, "No such scenario will happen."
The minister said he was hopeful about the IMF loan because the government was committed to greater fiscal discipline, natural resources management and civil service reform.
